endorsements.quote: Under FDA clinical decision support guidance, software that informs rather than replaces clinical judgment occupies a lower-risk regulatory tier [108], and the WHO and NIST AI governance frameworks anchor the system’s transparency, accountability, and fairness obligations [109], [110].

Maintaining knowledge as an explicit, queryable resource rather than relying on what a language model happens to recall is what allows the PCU to keep clinical guidance traceable to a verifiable source and updatable as evidence evolves.

fully auditing a continuously-evolving Personal Model will likely require versioned snapshots of the model state at the time of each decision, together with decision logs capturing the inputs, the attribution, and the chosen action.

unlisted_practices: Keep safety-critical clinical decisions as deterministic protocols that bypass personalization and LLM reasoning, and do not let user preferences or learned configuration override clinical safety thresholds.
Evaluate AI benefit and risk across demographic groups rather than only on average.
Design AI health tools to degrade gracefully with minimal sensors and to adapt to literacy level and multiple languages to avoid amplifying disparities.
Evaluate per-decision personalization with microrandomized trials and evaluate long-term outcomes with prospective cohort designs compared against threshold-based baselines.
Structurally separate clinical decision logic, behavioral strategy selection, and natural-language expression so LLMs handle communication and reasoning but not safety-critical clinical decisions.

screen.reason: This paper presents an architectural framework and blueprint proposal (Personal Care Utility) rather than an empirical evaluation on real clinical data or patient trials.
